item.title: Tojinbo Cliffs: Dramatic Basalt Formations Along the Sea of Japan — Guide
item.description: Tojinbo is a roughly 1-kilometre stretch of towering basalt cliffs along the Sea of Japan coast, designated a Natural Monument and considered one of only three such large-scale basalt cliff formations in the world, formed over millions of years by volcanic activity and subsequent erosion. Visitors can walk along clifftop paths for dramatic views down to the pounding surf below, or take a short pleasure boat tour that circles beneath the cliffs for a close-up perspective of the towering rock columns from sea level.
